title: Neural segmentation reveals persistent postsynaptic-density enlargement after potentiation
summary: In hippocampal slice neurons, StarDist neural-network segmentation identified postsynaptic densities for tracking over 16 hours. After CaMKII photoactivation, postsynaptic densities and spine heads enlarged rapidly; density enlargement persisted at 14 hours while spine-head expansion lasted about 6 hours. The original result was publicly posted on April 11, 2026, followed by a peer-reviewed version on November 20. The journal analysis included 6 activated and 5 control slice cultures, with thousands of nested synaptic measurements. Models were trained on a small manually annotated tile set and visually checked; held-out segmentation accuracy and independent replication were not reported.
ai_technology: StarDist convolutional neural network for star-convex image segmentation, adapted to PSD microscopy

evidence.tested: StarDist-based segmentation identified PSDs in activated and control hippocampal-slice microscopy time series, with 6 activated and 5 control slice cultures and 2,948/2,953 PSD objects in the reported comparison. The model-supported imaging showed PSD enlargement remained significant at 14 hours, whereas spine-head expansion lasted about 6 hours.
evidence.unknown: Only a small manually annotated tile set was used for model training; predictions were inspected/retrained, but a held-out segmentation-accuracy metric is not reported. PSD counts are repeated objects nested within 11 slice cultures, not independent biological replicates. No independent replication is reported.
evidence.ai_role: Custom StarDist neural-network models segmented PSD microscopy, followed by Mastodon temporal tracking and fluorescence-based quantification of PSD/spine changes. Learned segmentation contributed to the structural time course; separate electrophysiological pathway results were not produced by this model.

source_review.scope: Actual bioRxiv v1 and journal full text: StarDist training/segmentation and Mastodon tracking Methods, Fig1 and morphology time course, first-preprint posted date, journal sample counts/affiliation; original StarDist primary abstract for learned-model identity.
